newsitem.title: CANADA: Sale of Videotron's U.K. assets seen soon.
newsitem.headline: Sale of Videotron's U.K. assets seen soon.

text.p: The sale of Groupe Videotron Ltee's U.K. assets, Videotron Holdings Plc, is believed to be imminent, analysts said on Monday.
On Sunday, two British newspapers reported that Bell Cablemedia Plc or Cable and Wireless Plc was close to acquiring control of Videotron Holdings in a 600 million stg transaction.
A spokesman at BCE Inc's Bell Canada International unit, the parent company of Bell Cablemedia, declined to comment on the reports. Videotron officials did not return phone calls Monday.

Analysts have been expecting Bell Cablemedia to be involved in a transaction for Videotron Holdings since Groupe Videotron said in early February that it would consider offers for its 56.2 percent stake in the U.K. television cable network operator.
Ben Dube, analyst at Credifinance Securities Ltd, said a deal valued at 600 stg, or about US$23 a share, would be much higher than the US$17 a share price he was expecting.
On Nasdaq, Videotron Holdings ADRs were trading on Monday at 18, up 1/4 from Friday, while Bell Cablemedia was at 14-1/8, down from 14-1/2 Friday.
On the Montreal Exchange, shares of Groupe Videotron were up 0.20 to 11.10.
Even at US$17 a share in a cash and stock offer, the transaction would significantly improve Groupe Videotron's balance sheet.
"I think it's going to be fantastic for Videotron," Dube said.

Videotron has net debt of C$1.8 billion, including about C$600 million of debt at its U.K. cable operations. A price of US$17 a share for Videotron Holdings -- half paid in cash and the rest in Bell Cablemedia shares -- would cut Videotron's net debt by more than half to about C$1 billion.
An all-cash offer would cut Videotron's debt to about C$700 million.
A transaction involving shares of Bell Cablemedia could roughly double its shares outstanding, resulting in a significant dilution of that company's stock, Dube said.
"If this transaction works, it means of lot of dilution for Bell Cablemedia," he said.
That could explain why Bell Cablemedia's share price has fluctuated widely from a high of 18.50 earlier in the year. It fell as low as 12.50 before rebounding to about 16. It is currently at 14.50.
Bell Cablemedia and its partners in the transaction, if any, cannot fund the purchase with cash raised for developing Videotron's U.K. cable network, so it must raise additional financing.

Another plus for Groupe Videotron, aside from improving its balance sheet, was that a cash and share offer from Bell Cablemedia would mean that Groupe Videotron would become an important shareholder in the BCE unit.
-- Reuters Montreal bureau (514) 985-2434
But there was speculation that the announcement of a transaction was delayed beyond the end of August target date due partly to the complicated ownership links between the companies involved.
Bell Cablemedia owns 26.2 percent of Videotron Holdings. C&W holds 13 percent of Bell Cablemedia.
The sale of Groupe Videotron's U.K. assets would have important fiancial implications for the companies involved, whatever the price and structure of the transaction.
